title.en: Joint ventures and public private partnership

hook.en: An Indian two-wheeler maker and a Japanese engineering firm once joined hands to make motorcycles. Today many airports and highways are built by government and *private* companies together.

body.en: A *joint* venture is formed when two or more independent firms come together for a specific purpose. In a contractual joint venture they cooperate under an agreement without creating a new entity; in an equity-based joint venture they form a new business which they own jointly. Benefits include increased resources and capacity, access to new markets and distribution networks, access to technology, innovation, lower cost of production and an established brand name.

points.en: Equity-based JV: new jointly owned entity
Benefits: resources, markets, technology, innovation, low cost, brand name

problem.en: An Indian firm and a German firm form a new company, IndoGerm Pvt Ltd, investing ₹60 crore and ₹40 crore. Profit in year 1 is ₹15 crore, shared in the ratio of capital. What type of JV is this, and what is each partner's share?

steps.en: A new jointly owned entity is created: equity-based joint venture.
Indian firm = 15 × 3/5 = ₹9 crore; German firm = 15 × 2/5 = ₹6 crore.

narration.en: Let us work through this case together. An Indian firm and a German firm form a new company, IndoGerm Pvt Ltd, investing ₹60 crore and ₹40 crore. Profit in year 1 is ₹15 crore, shared in the ratio of capital. What type of JV is this, and what is each partner's share?

say.en: Let us work through this case together. An Indian firm and a German firm form a new company, IndoGerm Pvt Ltd, investing 60 rupees crore and 40 rupees crore. Profit in year 1 is 15 rupees crore, shared in the ratio of capital. What type of JV is this, and what is each partner's share?
A new jointly owned entity is created: equity-based joint venture.
Capital ratio equals 60: 40 equals 3: 2.
Indian firm equals 15 times 3 over 5 equals 9 rupees crore; German firm equals 15 times 2 over 5 equals 6 rupees crore.
So the answer is Equity-based JV; 9 rupees crore and 6 rupees crore.
